text:
maria: Heads-up — CI on main went red during the nightly run. Failure looks like a flaky unit in the serving runtime: `serving::test_retry_policy_race`. PR #1284 touched retry code earlier today. Job: https://ci.redwood/tests/112233 (commit: 0f4b2e7)

dev-cicd-bot: CI detected failure in `serving::test_retry_policy_race` (job 112233). Logs uploaded: https://ci.redwood/logs/112233

ryan: Can someone rerun the job quick? This one looks timing-y, might pass on retry.

bob: kicked a rerun -> still failing, same stack trace.

maria: attaching the failing assertion from the test run:
```
thread 'tokio-runtime-worker' panicked at 'expected retry_count == 2, got 3', runtime/src/retry/mod.rs:142:21
stack backtrace:
  at runtime::retry::backoff::exponential
  at runtime::serve::handler::handle_request
  ...
```

carol: Any recent changes that touch backoff/timers? I glanced at PR #1284 and it touched `retry.rs` but it was supposed to be refactor-only.

dave: Looks like the test relies on real timers + Tokio delays. Flake could come from scheduler noise. Suggest running locally with tokio's time control or set `TEST_RUST_THREADS=1` to reduce scheduling variance.

ryan: Good call. Locally I was able to reproduce with `RUST_LOG=info TEST_SEED=12345 cargo test serving::test_retry_policy_race -- --nocapture` — the seed changes behavior. We should try a bisect between `abc1234` (yesterday) and `0f4b2e7` (failing commit) to narrow it down.

maria: Can someone run a quick git bisect? If it's nondeterministic we might need to run the test multiple times per commit.

bob: I'll start a bisect job with script to run the test 5 times per commit and mark bad if any run fails. Command I'm using:
```
git bisect start 0f4b2e7 abc1234
# then for each commit:
RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 sh -c 'for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do TEST_SEED=$RANDOM cargo test serving::test_retry_policy_race --quiet && continue || exit 1; done'
# git bisect good/bad accordingly
```

dev-cicd-bot: Note: running bisect on CI will use shared workers — might get noisy results. Prefer running on a pinned VM or local reproducible env.

carol: If bisect narrows to a refactor commit that didn't change semantics, the culprit may be the test itself relying on wall-clock timings. We should consider rewriting the test to use time mocking: `tokio::time::pause()` + `tokio::time::advance()` so it's deterministic.

maria: Agreed. Short term, let's mark the test as flaky in CI thresholds and add an issue to refactor the test harness. Longer term, convert to mocked timers. I can open the issue and a follow-up PR.

ryan: Also propose adding a small guard: in `retry.rs` avoid tight coupling to real-time in unit tests by exposing an injectable `sleep_fn` or `Clock` trait. That makes tests easier to control.

dave: For immediate unblock, I pushed a temporary revert of the small refactor in PR #1284 (branch: revert/1284-timer-guard) to see if CI stabilizes. Not ideal but buys time.

bob: Re-run CI against that revert branch now? I kicked it — pending.

dev-cicd-bot: CI job 112241 started for branch `revert/1284-timer-guard`.

maria: Thanks all. Action items: (1) bob to finish bisect run and report commit range, (2) carol + ryan to prototype a mocked-timer version of the test, (3) maria to file issue and track PR to remove flakiness. If bisect points to an actual bug in retry logic, we'll prioritize a fix instead of test-only change.

carol: I'll post bisect updates in this thread. If anyone reproduces locally, drop the `TEST_SEED` you used so we can correlate.

ryan: FYI my local seeds that reproduced: 12345, 19876. Adding to the issue.

maria: Closing loop — revert branch CI passed so far (looks stable). Still want bisect to ensure we didn't hide a bug. Thanks :thumbsup:
